Incumbent Governor [[Tom Wolf]] won a second term by a double-digit margin, defeating [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] challenger [[Scott Wagner]] and two third-party candidates, [[Paul Glover (activist)|Paul Glover]] from the [[Green Party of the United States|Green Party]], and Ken Krawchuk from the [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian Party]].{{cite web|url=http://www.politicspa.com/pa-gov-wolf-i-am-running-for-re-election-in-2018/82004|title=Pa-Gov: Wolf: 'I am running for re-election in 2018'|publisher=PoliticsPA|date=March 7, 2017|access-date=June 15, 2017}}{{cite news |url=https://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/news/politics/Pennsylvania-Governor-Race-Tom-Wolf-Scott-Wagner-Election-Results-2018-499854871.html |publisher=[[WCAU]] |date=November 6, 2018 |title=Tom Wolf Is the Projected Winner of a Second Term as Pennsylvania Governor, Defeating Republican Challenger Scott Wagner |access-date=November 7, 2018}} The primary elections were held on May 15.{{cite web |url=http://www.ncsl.org/research/elections-and-campaigns/2018-state-primary-election-dates.aspx |title=State Primary Election Dates |website=National Conference of State Legislatures |date=January 10, 2018 |access-date=November 7, 2018 |archive-date=April 20, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180420154714/http://www.ncsl.org/research/elections-and-campaigns/2018-state-primary-election-dates.aspx |url-status=dead }} This was the only Democratic-held governorship up for election in a state that [[Donald Trump]] won in the [[2016 United States presidential election|2016 presidential election]]. Wagner won eight counties that Wolf won in 2014: [[Lawrence County, Pennsylvania|Lawrence]], [[Greene County, Pennsylvania|Greene]], [[Fayette County, Pennsylvania|Fayette]], [[Cambria County, Pennsylvania|Cambria]], [[Clinton County, Pennsylvania|Clinton]], [[Northumberland County, Pennsylvania|Northumberland]], [[Carbon County, Pennsylvania|Carbon]], and [[Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania|Schuylkill]].
